memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So Joshua called together the twelve men he had appointed from the Israelites, one from each tribe, and said to them, "Go over before the ark of the Lord your God into the middle of the Jordan. Each of you is to take up a stone on his shoulder, according to the number of the tribes of the Israelites." — Josh 4:4-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joshua chose one man from each of the twelve tribes to carry a stone. Not one leader for all, not a random dozen, but a representative from every single tribe. God wanted the whole nation included in this memorial. No tribe was left out; each had a hand in remembering God's faithfulness.

There is a lovely picture of the family of God here. Every tribe mattered. Every part of the community was represented. God's work was not for a special few while the rest watched; it belonged to all of them together. When God does something great, He weaves the whole community into it.

Notice too that each man carried his stone "on his shoulder." This was personal, physical, involving effort. Remembering God's faithfulness is not always effortless; sometimes it takes deliberate labour to build the reminders that keep faith alive. But that shoulder-borne stone became part of something lasting.

The church today is like those twelve tribes — many members, from every background, each with a part to play (1 Cor 12:12). No believer is a spare part. Christ has drawn people from every tribe and tongue into one body (Rev 5:9), and each of us carries our own "stone," contributing to the shared testimony of what God has done.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you see yourself as an included, contributing member of God's family?
2. What deliberate effort can you make to "carry a stone" — to remember and testify to God's work?
3. How does it encourage you that God includes every kind of person in His purposes?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for including me in Your family and Your work. Help me carry my part faithfully alongside my brothers and sisters. Amen.
